report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Run node ids with solo re-runs, validate task schema, manage disposable worktrees, apply test overlays and reference patches, and define the frozen Selection dataclass.

symbols.name: run_node_ids
symbols.note: Runs pytest on given node ids in a worktree, re-running unattributed nodes solo; returns PytestRun.

symbols.name: TestRunner
symbols.note: Type alias for injectable test runner callable.

symbols.name: REQUIRED_FIELDS
symbols.note: Tuple of required task dict fields: id, repo, base_revision, fail_to_pass.

symbols.name: validate_task
symbols.note: Returns list of schema problems for a task dict; never raises.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task.

symbols.name: disposable_worktree
symbols.note: Context manager creating a git worktree via GitWorktreeManager; cleans up unless keep=True.

symbols.name: apply_test_overlay
symbols.note: Writes test files from test_revision into worktree via git show; raises FileNotFoundError or OverlayEscape.

symbols.name: reference_patch
symbols.note: Returns git diff base..reference as bytes, excluding given paths.

symbols.name: apply_patch
symbols.note: Applies patch bytes in worktree via git apply; returns None or error reason.

symbols.name: Selection
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass capturing measurement selection; includes to_dict method.

symbols.name: Selection.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict of selection fields including argv_shape and digest.

claims.text: Run exactly these node ids inside ``worktree`` and attribute per node.
claims.why: The function builds argv from the given node_ids, runs pytest via _spawn_pytest, and parses output to attribute statuses per node.

claims.text: Batch first (one interpreter start, ~2.2s on this box, measured), then RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed.
claims.why: The code runs the full batch first, then iterates over unattributed nodes and calls _spawn_pytest for each solo.

claims.text: That fallback is not belt-and-braces, it is required: measured on this box, a single node id pytest cannot collect aborts the WHOLE invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs -- even with ``--continue-on-collection-errors``.
claims.why: The claim cites measurements and pytest behaviour; this chunk only shows the fallback implementation, not the measurement or the absence of --continue-on-collection-errors in pytest_node_argv.

claims.text: Without the solo re-run, one bad node id would turn every other node in the batch into ``not_run`` and the task into ``could_not_run``.
claims.why: This is a hypothetical consequence; the code only shows the solo re-run logic, not what happens without it.

claims.text: ``worktree`` is refused if it is the primary checkout or inside it.
claims.why: The function calls _refuse_primary_checkout(worktree, repo_root, ...) on the first line of its body.

claims.text: An EMPTY ``fail_to_pass`` is an error, not an empty success: a task with no test that must go from red to green cannot fail, and a measurement that cannot fail is the exact defect ``harness._recall``'s vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: The function checks REQUIRED_FIELDS including fail_to_pass; if it is missing or empty, it appends 'missing or empty required field'. There is no special-casing that would accept an empty list.

claims.text: Every schema problem with ``task``, or ``[]``. Never raises.
claims.why: The function returns a list and uses .get() for all accesses; it never indexes the dict directly, and it returns early for non-dict input.

claims.text: The same node id is in both lists: ... it cannot both fail and pass before the change
claims.why: The function computes the intersection of fail_to_pass and pass_to_pass and reports it as a problem.

claims.text: True for a task carrying the correctness format. Mirrored in ``daedalus.eval.tasks`` so the harness can refuse to grade one with substring recall; defined there, re-exported here for callers who already have this module imported.
claims.why: The function imports and delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task, matching the described mirror.

claims.text: A checkout of ``revision`` that is NOT the primary checkout.
claims.why: The function creates a worktree via GitWorktreeManager and then calls _refuse_primary_checkout on the resulting path, which enforces the non-primary requirement.

claims.text: Delegates to :class:`daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager` on purpose rather than shelling out to ``git worktree add``
claims.why: The code instantiates GitWorktreeManager and calls its create_worktree method; it does not invoke git worktree add directly.

claims.text: Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no ``shutil.rmtree`` here and there must never be one.
claims.why: Within this chunk, the only deletion is via manager.cleanup_worktree and manager.reap_branches; no shutil.rmtree is present.

claims.text: The branch ref that ``git worktree add -b`` writes into the shared ``.git`` is reaped afterwards through the manager's own ``reap_branches``, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.
claims.why: The chunk shows the call to manager.reap_branches(), but the claim about what reap_branches deletes and its conditions is inside GitWorktreeManager, not visible here.

claims.text: Write the task's test files, as of ``test_revision``, into the worktree.
claims.why: The function runs git show test_revision:rel and writes the output to target in the worktree.

claims.text: This is SWE-bench's "test patch", and it is what makes a before-state measurable at all: the base revision predates the fix, so it also predates the fix's tests -- running a FAIL_TO_PASS node against a bare base checkout would only ever report ``missing``.
claims.why: This describes the conceptual role; the code only implements the overlay write, not the before-state measurement.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (``git show <rev>:<path>``), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
claims.why: The function uses proc.stdout (raw bytes) and target.write_bytes(proc.stdout), avoiding any text decoding.

claims.text: Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` if a path does not exist at that revision, and :class:`OverlayEscape` if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: The code raises FileNotFoundError when git show returns non-zero; OverlayEscape is raised by _safe_join, which is called for each rel before writing.

claims.text: The known-good change as a patch: ``git diff base..reference``.
claims.why: The function constructs git diff arguments with base_revision and reference_revision and returns proc.stdout.

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the "after" run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: The function appends :(exclude) pathspecs for each entry in the exclude sequence to the git diff command.

claims.text: Apply ``patch_bytes`` inside the worktree. Returns None, or the reason.
claims.why: The function writes patch_bytes to a temp file and runs git apply; returns None on success or a reason string on failure.

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a ``could_not_run``, never a ``not_fixed``: "the change was rejected by git" and "the change did not fix the bug" are different facts about different things.
claims.why: The function returns an error string for a failed apply, but the mapping of that to could_not_run vs not_fixed is in the caller, not in this chunk.

claims.text: WHAT WILL BE MEASURED, fixed before any candidate code runs.
claims.why: The dataclass is frozen and holds all measurement parameters; it is constructed before candidate code runs by the caller (not shown here, but the design is consistent).

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so "what was measured is what was declared" is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring.
claims.why: The class is decorated with @dataclass(frozen=True) and uses tuple fields for fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, and test_overlay; it has a digest attribute referenced in to_dict.

claims.text: Everything a result depends on is in here: both node id lists, the RESOLVED base sha (not the ref that was typed), the overlay revision and paths, and the gate configuration.
claims.why: The dataclass fields include base_revision, fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, test_revision, test_overlay, gate, and timeout_s, but whether base_revision is the RESOLVED sha is determined by the caller when constructing the Selection; not visible here.

claims.text: ``digest`` covers all of it. Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes, which is what lets :func:`correctness_gate` refuse a task that was verified under one selection and presented under another.
claims.why: The chunk references self.digest in to_dict but does not show its computation; correctness_gate is in another chunk.

observations.what: The solo re-run loop does not update the overall returncode or argv to reflect the solo runs; it only appends solo output and sets timed_out/containment. The final PytestRun uses the batch rc and argv, which may be misleading if solo runs succeeded or failed differently.
observations.what would settle it: Check whether the caller interprets returncode and argv as batch-only or as overall; the docstring says 'attribute per node' and the statuses are per-node, but rc is not per-node.

observations.what: The solo re-run loop treats containment as 'none' only if the batch containment is 'none'; otherwise it keeps the batch containment, even if a solo run had a different containment status. This may under-report containment from solo runs.
observations.what would settle it: Inspect the containment semantics in _spawn_pytest and how callers use it.

observations.what: In apply_test_overlay, the code writes directly to target.write_bytes without first checking that target is inside the worktree; it relies on _safe_join to enforce that, which is a separate function not shown in this chunk. The docstring claims OverlayEscape is raised, and _safe_join is listed as existing, so the claim is likely kept, but the enforcement is external.
observations.what would settle it: Read _safe_join's implementation to confirm it raises OverlayEscape for escapes.

observations.what: apply_patch creates a temporary file with delete=False and deletes it in a finally block; if the subprocess.run times out or raises an unexpected exception, the file is still unlinked because the finally block runs. However, the patch file is written with default permissions and could be a security concern if the worktree is shared; not a correctness issue.
observations.what would settle it: Review the security context of the temp file; the code uses tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with default permissions.

observations.what: The Selection.to_dict method includes 'argv_shape' computed from pytest_node_argv(('<node>',)), which is a shape descriptor, not the actual argv used for a specific run. The digest is referenced but not computed in this chunk.
observations.what would settle it: Check the digest property implementation in another part of the file.

observations.what: validate_task checks that fail_to_pass and pass_to_pass entries contain '::', but it does not validate that test_overlay entries are valid paths or that test_revision is a valid revision; it only checks that test_overlay requires test_revision. This could allow malformed overlay paths to slip through.
observations.what would settle it: Inspect the task schema documentation or downstream usage to see if path validation is expected.

risks: run_node_ids | medium | Overall returncode and argv reflect the batch run, not solo re-runs; a solo failure could be misreported as a batch success. | Check how callers interpret the returncode field of PytestRun in the context of solo re-runs.

run_node_ids | low | Containment from solo runs is ignored unless the batch containment is 'none'; solo containment could be lost. | Inspect the containment semantics and whether solo containment should override batch containment.

apply_test_overlay | low | OverlayEscape enforcement is delegated to _safe_join, which is not visible in this chunk; if _safe_join is faulty, the claim is broken. | Read _safe_join's implementation to confirm it raises OverlayEscape on escape.
apply_patch | low | Temp file permissions are default; if the worktree is shared, the patch could be readable by others. | Review the security context and consider using a more restrictive file mode.

Selection.to_dict | low | argv_shape is a static shape, not the actual argv; digest computation is not shown, so the claim that digest covers all fields is unverified. | Inspect the digest property implementation and confirm it includes all fields.
validate_task | low | Overlay paths are not validated for existence or format; only test_revision presence is checked. | Determine if downstream code expects path validation.

apply_patch | low | The patch is applied with --whitespace=nowarn, which may mask whitespace errors that could be relevant to the evaluation. | Check the project's policy on whitespace handling in patches.

disposable_worktree | low | The branch name includes a UUID, but reap_branches is called only in the finally block; if cleanup_worktree raises, reap_branches is still called because of the nested finally, but if reap_branches itself raises, it is caught and ignored. This is by design but could leak branches if reap_branches has a bug. | Inspect GitWorktreeManager.reap_branches for robustness.

run_node_ids | low | The function deduplicates node_ids but preserves order; if duplicate node ids are passed, they are run once, but the output may not clearly indicate that duplicates were collapsed. | Check if the caller expects duplicates to be preserved or reported.

validate_task | low | The function checks for '::' in node ids but does not validate the path portion; a node id like '::test_y' would pass the check. | Determine if the format check is sufficient for the task schema.
